title: Multi-planet chain reaction may have sparked life on Earth: Avi Loeb
excerpt: University of Cambridge astronomers have ruled out a longstanding theory.
content:
Jesse Weber

Updated Fri, November 6, 2026 at 9:43 AM UTC

(NewsNation) — New research rejects the theory that comets delivered life-generating chemical compounds to Earth, but Mars may have been successfully infused by comets before asteroids from the Red Planet landed on Earth, says Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb.

“It teaches us a sense of cosmic modesty: Things that are far more impressive than what we are trying to accomplish with our technologies were done by nature billions of years ago,” Loeb told “Jesse Weber Live” on Thursday.

Was Mars ‘pyramid’ alien-made? Red Planet authority weighs in

In a study published last week, University of Cambridge astronomers said models they ran ruled out the conventional idea that comets — known as the “dirty snowballs” of space — helped seed the Earth with the first forms of life. Researchers say organic payloads on comets would have been destroyed on their way in but may have survived when striking the smaller Mars.

It's possible that other delivery systems, including asteroids, may have sparked life on Earth, the study says.

“Obviously, if you establish life on Mars early enough, that could have been delivered to Earth through asteroids. We know that rocks could survive the conditions of entering through the Earth’s atmosphere if they come from Mars,” Loeb said.

Scientists have identified hundreds of meteorites from Mars on our planet.

Although scholars have theorized that life’s building blocks arrived by comets or asteroids, another school of thought is that Earth already had the necessary ingredients for what developed.
